title: ÆTHER: The Oath v2 (prompt mode, music_v2)
story: A warrior swears an oath at a lamp-lit temple at night, knowing it will cost him his life. He keeps it, and a hundred voices carry his name after him.

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct: an emotional sacrifice theme, a solo flute that rises to a full choir; he rejected Monsoon Duel as 'nothing unique', so uniqueness is the first job. What makes it ours: (1) the whole track walks in a 7-beat cycle (misra chapu, 3+2+2) instead of the usual 4/4, so the pulse limps like a heartbeat carrying a weight; (2) the flute's own breath is chopped into the rhythm (Broken Heritage: breath chiffs and key clicks as glitch percussion); (3) a heartbeat that is the kick drum and STOPS at the sacrifice; (4) a temple bell struck three times for the three vows; (5) the choir grows from one hummed voice to a hundred, never a choir pad from the start. Rules 9.1-9.14: one sound alone at first, layer by layer, a composed hook at every change every 8-12 s, about half real instruments, a key lift, a full silence and a slam, the motif at both ends. v1 (plan mode fell back to music_v1) measured: both takes repeat every 3.2 s = plain 4/4 at 76 BPM (the 7-beat cycle was ignored), takes open with 1-3 s of silence, and the heartbeat stop at the sacrifice was a 2 s dip, not a stop. v2 tries prompt mode on music_v2, which follows sound and feel better.

prompt: Emotional, goosebump-raising cinematic sacrifice theme, instrumental, 72 seconds, about 76 BPM, in an odd 7/8 meter (7 beats per bar grouped 3+2+2, a limping heartbeat pulse, never 4/4). It opens at second zero with one deep temple bell strike and a low boom, then a lone, close, breathy Indian bamboo flute plays a rising 3-note call (root, minor third, fifth, last note bent upward) over a soft drone. The flute's own breath puffs and key clicks are chopped into glitchy rhythmic percussion in 7/8, and a deep human heartbeat is the kick. A sad, singable flute melody in a minor raga with Carnatic slides; a cello answers it, a warm analog synth bass moves under it, mridangam and big cinematic drums join one layer at a time, low brass and climbing violins, and a wordless choir that grows from one hummed female voice to ten voices. Around 40 seconds everything stops: the heartbeat slows and stops, one second of total silence, the lone flute plays the theme broken and slow with a temple bell. Then a reversed veena swell into a massive slam: a huge hundred-voice choir sings the theme a whole step higher with full drums, brass and strings in 7/8, the flute soaring above. Ends on a huge chord and sub drop, then the lone flute plays the rising 3-note call once more, ringing into silence. About half real instruments, half warm fresh electronics; clean, wide, warm, glossy mix. No EDM drop, no risers, no vocals with words.
